Adjacent eight-unit filings are six days apart and share the same applicant, reported condominium-lot site, scale, and description.
The 32- and six-unit buildings share a named owner, applicant, site BBL, seven-story design, and permits.
Adjacent eight-unit buildings were filed two days apart and share the same applicant, site BBL, scale, and description.
Six same-day seven-unit filings have sequential addresses and lots and share one named owner, applicant, site BBL, and design.
Same-day 84- and 213-unit filings share a named owner, applicant, site BBL, eleven-story design, and permits.
Adjacent eight- and six-unit buildings share a named owner, applicant, site BBL, design, and issued certificates of occupancy.

Same-day adjacent six-unit filings share a named owner, applicant, site BBL, design, and permits.
Same-day 386- and 460-unit buildings have related Phase 1 owner entities, one applicant, a common site BBL, and permits.

The filings are 238 days apart, have different owners and applicants, describe different four- and five-story buildings, and the earlier adjacent-lot filing was withdrawn before the later building received a certificate of occupancy.
Adjacent six-unit buildings share an applicant, site BBL, nearly identical descriptions, and permits; the first filing lacks a usable named owner.
The DOB zoning diagram labels the five job numbers Buildings A through E on one development lot; all five propose 99 units and are linked by exact adjacency or the site BBL.
Adjacent filings share the same named owner and applicant, common site BBL, similar four-story descriptions, and approval status.
The 99+99+70 filings share a named owner, applicant, site BBL, eleven-story design, and dates within seven days; NYSDEC identifies all addresses as one remediation site.

The 61-unit filing explicitly says it is filed in conjunction with the 71-unit job; both share an applicant, site BBL, design, and permits.

The initial 70- and 60-unit filings explicitly reference one another but were withdrawn; the later 99-unit filing on the same site received the permit and financing, so the three filings are one economic parent but not additive.
The 77-, 84-, and 94-unit filings share a named owner, applicant, site BBL, coherent block addresses, and related nine- to twelve-story designs.
The paired 84-unit buildings share a named owner, applicant, site BBL, identical twelve-story design, and approval status.
The 73-unit filing explicitly references the adjacent 60-unit job and states that the zoning lots share the same owner and applicant.
Three same-day 82- to 87-unit filings share a named owner, applicant, coherent block addresses, and closely related building descriptions.
The 88+99+99 filings share a named owner, applicant, site BBL, eight-story design, sequential Far Rockaway Boulevard addresses, and active approval or permit status.
Same-day 86- and 39-unit buildings share a named owner, applicant, site BBL, eight-story design, and two sides of one development site.
The 268- and 792-unit filings are five days apart and share an applicant, site BBL, private-owner coding, Dev Hub consultation, and adjacent Greenpoint waterfront addresses.
Four 99-unit filings share a named owner, applicant, site BBL, fourteen-story description, and dates within 26 days; the state brownfield agreement identifies the addresses as one property.
Each filing explicitly names the other and states that the two buildings occupy one zoning lot with one owner and applicant.
Same-day attached eight-unit buildings have adjacent addresses and lots and share one applicant, site BBL, scale, and description.
Both same-day filings identify MPP project 000000563 and share a named owner, applicant, site BBL, and adjacent addresses.
Seven same-day 99-unit filings share one named owner, applicant, site BBL, and parallel descriptions; The Real Deal independently reports seven planned buildings at the site.
Three same-day buildings share Phipps Houses, Dattner Architects, one site BBL, and distinct building scales and addresses; two buildings may share one tax lot without being alternative filings.
Same-day Building 5 and Building 6 LIHTC owner entities share an applicant, reported project BBL, adjacent Flatlands Avenue addresses, and distinct 13- and 14-story buildings.

The current four-filing parent combines independent developers: ZD Jasper's 99-unit lot-13 project and EMP Capital's neighboring lot-16/18 project. Reporting identifies EMP's current pair as 99 and 77 units, making its earlier 79-unit same-lot filing a superseded alternative.
